body:
`load-plugin.sh`'s `build_tag` helper can include hexadecimal characters from the next linked string in the commit hash. Observed while validating PR #1429 on Linux at `de2774e5`.

Reproduction:
1. Build the plugin in that PR with `cargo build --release -p harmonigraph-plugin -p harmonigraph-offline`.
2. Invoke the existing `build_tag` function on `target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.so` with branch `codex/shadow-blur-preview` (the wrapper only locates `.dylib` files).
3. It prints `codex/shadow-blur-preview @de2774e5a`; the actual stamped tag is `codex/shadow-blur-preview @de2774e5`.

The binary contains adjacent bytes `codex/shadow-blur-preview @de2774e5a formatting trait implementation return`. The plugin build-script output records the shorter tag. The branch prefix is already anchored, but `[0-9a-f]{7,40}` greedily consumes the next string's initial `a`.

No loader changes were made in the shadow PR. A durable fix should delimit the embedded tag or otherwise read its recorded length, with a fixture whose next string starts with hex characters. Whether this layout also occurs in the macOS dylib remains unverified.
title: Build tag reader can consume hex characters from the next linked string

body:
The build-tag extractor in `load-plugin.sh` can consume a hexadecimal prefix from the next string in a Rust binary. This was observed while validating the Linux build of #1427; no loader changes were made in that PR.

At `f0af8f2c`, the plugin build-script output records `LATTICE_BUILD_TAG=codex/inline-temperaments @f0af8f2c`. The `.so` contains the bytes `codex/inline-temperaments @f0af8f2ca formatting trait implementation returned an error...`, where the final `a` begins the following string. The loader's extraction expression (`@[0-9a-f]{7,40}`) consequently reports `@f0af8f2ca`.

Reproduction: build the Linux plugin from #1427, then run the `strings -a` / branch-name regex pipeline from `build_tag()` against `target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.so`. Compare with `target/release/build/harmonigraph-plugin-*/output` and the literal bytes. The real tag is present; this is not a stale build or failed build-script rerun. `--tag` itself expects a macOS dylib, so the complete native macOS loader path has not been reproduced.

Likely fix: give the embedded tag an unambiguous terminator or read its exact length instead of treating adjacent string bytes as part of the SHA. Check the freshness comparison too, since it consumes the extracted SHA.
title: Build-tag extraction can consume adjacent hexadecimal string bytes

body:
The repository's lifecycle handoff declares `target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.dylib` as a required artifact on every platform.
A Linux cloud build produces `target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.so` instead, so the build succeeds but publication refuses the missing dylib.
The offline renderer is built successfully too; this is artifact selection, not a Rust build failure.

Reproduce in the configured Linux cloud checkout with the shared session-lifecycle tool installed:

```sh
./session-lifecycle.sh handoff
```

The configured build is `cargo build --release -p harmonigraph-plugin -p harmonigraph-offline`.
Observed on Linux x86-64 at `985b444fb832beb03bf678581c32c8bc87f7d716` (#1424), with shared lifecycle tool revision `920acd5`:

```text
Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 25.83s
lifecycle: required build output missing: /workspace/harmonigraph/target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.dylib
```

Both `target/release/libharmonigraph_plugin.so` and `target/release/harmonigraph-offline` are ELF x86-64 binaries.
The plugin's embedded build tag is `codex/sweep-view-ranges @985b444f`, read with the loader's own `build_tag` helper.
No preserved publication or cache pruning followed the refusal.

The helper's `publish` walks `.agent-lifecycle.json`'s literal `artifacts` list, without platform selection.
No artifact was renamed to disguise the platform, no manifest override was used, and the source/caches remain available after refusal.
The cloud handover still works through `./build-pr.sh --load 1424` on the owner's Mac, but Linux does not satisfy the new preserved-handoff contract.

Follow-up needs a supported per-platform artifact declaration in the shared lifecycle contract, or an explicit cloud completion route.
Found while sweeping #1408, whose final stage is #1424.
title: Lifecycle handoff cannot preserve Linux builds with the macOS-only artifact manifest

body:
Since #1337 and #1347, `star_geometry` (`crates/harmonigraph-render/src/stars.rs`) is a `Float4` whose x and y are written as 0.0, because each slice carries its own `width` and `inner`. Its z is the constant 0.7 (where a 3x3 star's inner part starts fading), and only w (`Distant gap fill`) varies.

It sits in two uniforms: `StarUniforms` and the spectrogram's `Cloud` (`shaders/spectrogram.wgsl`). Anyone reading `star_geometry().x` would get 0 rather than a band.

**Proposed:** make 0.7 a shader `const`, and carry far fill as one scalar lane. The two dead lanes then go away.

This is cosmetic, with no behaviour change. It costs a Metal corpus regeneration, so do it alongside the next star shader change rather than on its own.

Raised by the design review of #1347.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Stars: star_geometry carries two dead lanes and a constant

body:
Drift-from-intent audit of every area (`/audit-drift` with no area), run on `main` at 4655c5ee.
Each area had a blind describer (current code only) and an auditor (history and PRs).
Every finding was verified against `main` before it went anywhere.
Anything mechanical is in one grouped issue per area; only what needs your call is asked here.

**How to answer:** take any one area at a time and reply in a comment, e.g. `Stars: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 skip`.
Each question says what happens on either answer.
The session that receives your answers records them in `docs/intent/<area>.md`, ticks the row, and files what they call for.

## Two bugs, found in passing

- #1301: a project saved **with the editor open** stores the settings from the last editor close, not what is on screen. Found by reading; not yet reproduced in Bitwig.
- #1302: the Tuning pane's "Reset to recover" notice points at a Reset that does not clear Learn's latch.

## Index

Most consequential questions first.

| Area | Questions | Issues | Answered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Colors and MIDI note intensity](#colors-and-midi-note-intensity) | 2 | #1303 | 1 of 2 (Q1 fine) |
| [Lattice glow and bloom](#lattice-glow-and-bloom) | 1 | #1304 | ☑ #1315 |
| [Lattice notes, layout and motion](#lattice-notes-layout-and-motion) | 2 | #1305 | 1 of 2 (Q1 bug #1316) |
| [Stars texture](#stars-texture) | 4 | #1306 | 1 of 4 (Q1 intended) |
| [Video: takes and offline export](#video-takes-and-offline-export) | 3 | #1307 | ☐ |
| [Spectrogram textures](#spectrogram-textures) | 2 | #1308 | ☐ |
| [Spectrum analyzer and audio analysis](#spectrum-analyzer-and-audio-analysis) | 2 | #1309 | ☐ |
| [Lattice shadows and the idle lattice](#lattice-shadows-and-the-idle-lattice) | 2 | #1310 | ☐ |
| [Tuning, lattice maps and adaptive tuning](#tuning-lattice-maps-and-adaptive-tuning) | 1 | #1311, bug #1302 | ☐ |
| [Editor shell, layout and saved state](#editor-shell-layout-and-saved-state) | 1 | #1312, bug #1301 | ☐ |
| [Spiral](#spiral) | 1 | #1313 | ☐ |
| MIDI ribbons and their bloom | — | not re-audited | covered by the first trial's intent record |

## Area map

Correct these boundaries for the next run.

- **Colors and MIDI note intensity:** Mappings tab: pitch and level gradients, note intensity routing and its consumers.
- **Lattice glow and bloom:** Note bloom, Background glow, Glow pattern, Glow material (not Stars).
- **Lattice notes, layout and motion:** View/camera, Note layers, Octave layout, Note animation, Note labels, Audio ring, marks, trail.
- **Stars texture:** Stars in both the Analyzer and the Lattice, and Stars rendering quality.
- **Video: takes and offline export:** Video tab, take format, recorder, `harmonigraph-offline`.
- **Spectrogram textures:** Softness, contours, Mosaic, Watercolor, Scales, colour memory.
- **Spectrum analyzer and audio analysis:** Analyzer View and Analysis sections, the curve, history, FFT/fold pipeline.
- **Lattice shadows and the idle lattice:** Lattice Shadows section, crosses, idle brightness.
- **Tuning, lattice maps and adaptive tuning:** Tuning tab, Learn, Lattice Map engine, Hub and Tune.
- **Editor shell, layout and saved state:** Settings column, folds, docked panes, System tab, persistence.
- **Spiral:** The Spiral picture, Spiral bloom, its shadows and shared settings.
- **MIDI ribbons and their bloom:** skipped; the first trial just produced its intent record (#1289–#1297).

---

## Colors and MIDI note intensity (Mappings tab)

### Questions

1. **At the fresh settings, velocity only shows on very soft notes. Is that intended?**
   Fresh intensity routes velocity (0.61) and gain (0.51) to Opacity over a rest of 0.30, as captured from your DAW in #1205.
   A host sends gain at unity for a note with no gain lane, and since #1162 unity gain adds its whole weight.
   So every note starts at 0.81: anything above velocity ≈ 39/127 draws fully opaque, and the softest note draws at 81%.
   The Mappings preview hides this, because each source's band is drawn as if the others add nothing (the Velocity band reads 0.30→0.91).
   - *Yes:* record it, and retitle the fresh-defaults test (it runs at gain 0, which a host almost never sends) to state the common case.
   - *No:* drop gain from the fresh routes, or lower the rest, so velocity spans the range; check it against a take.
2. **Should the Spiral's note dots follow the Opacity mapping?**
   Today they use the note envelope only (`panes/spiral.rs:860`), so a note faded to nothing on the lattice and piano roll still draws a full dot on the Spiral.
   The Spiral was scoped out in #1133 by the #1130 handoff, the one that misstated the routing model.
   The Mappings page and `docs/settings.md` both say the mappings apply to "every picture".
   - *Yes:* read `IntensitySettings` in the Spiral's dots.
   - *No:* change the two "every picture" lines to "the lattice and the piano roll".

### Mechanical

Filed as #1303; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- The audio palette buttons (Ice, Aurora, Magma) don't reproduce the fresh audio gradient, which is a retuned Aurora with a late bend (#1205). Double-clicking a bar restores the fresh gradient.
- The audio ring's quiet end sits at **Idle ring brightness** rather than at the scheme's floor. This is deliberate, and the UI says so.

---

## Lattice glow and bloom

### Questions

1. **Should a soft note's Background glow dim with its Opacity, as its ink and bloom do?**
   Fresh settings route velocity and gain to Opacity, but the halo follows the note's plain envelope (`scene/motion.rs:683`).
   So a soft or low-gain note draws a faint slice under a full-strength halo.
   #1133 decoupled the two because Glow was then a routable display of its own. #1166 removed that route and left the decoupling without a reason.
   You decided in #1289 that ribbon bloom follows Opacity; lattice bloom already does, through the ink.
   - *Yes:* restore the pre-#1133 target (the drawn ink), which also fixes the colour-history mismatch below. As with bloom, a node's halo then follows its most opaque slice.
   - *No:* record it, fix the colour-history mismatch on its own, and correct the two docs that say otherwise.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1304; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- The node glow's gather and p-norm union are gone: #877/#879 replaced them with half-resolution halo quads and one resolve pass.
- Note bloom also blooms the Background glow's core, as it has since #437. You tuned the two together.

---

## Lattice notes, layout and motion

### Questions

1. **Should a note's name, and the cross it replaces, ignore how softly the note was played?**
   Under Label visibility History (fresh), the first time a pitch class is played softly its name is drawn at the note's opacity, say 0.6, while the key is held, and the cross under it stands at 0.4.
   At key-up the name jumps to full and the cross vanishes in one frame.
   #434 reserved a departing name at 1.0 on the premise that a held note is at 1. #1133 made a held note carry its opacity, and fresh settings route velocity to opacity.
   - *Yes:* the name level reads the unfaded envelope; the grey-to-white ink can still follow opacity.
   - *No:* make the departing reserve ramp from the held level instead of jumping to 1.
2. **Should Note fade, Ring threshold and Ring attack/release get their explanations back?**
   #1278 (merged 2026-09-29) put them in compact diagrams and dropped their hover texts:
   - what Note fade covers (slices, marks, labels and ring visibility), and that a release during the arrival reverses;
   - "MIDI notes always show their rings" on the threshold;
   - that the ring times come after Live attack/release on the Analyzer.
   The PR listed what it kept (saved keys, automation), not the help text. `panes/nodes.rs:98` still says "Both are in the hover text".
   - *Yes:* hang them on the diagrams' hover.
   - *No:* delete the `nodes.rs` claim; `docs/settings.md` keeps Note fade's scope.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1305; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- The Audio ring is off in a fresh view (width 0). With it on, widening Audio past about 0.15 pushes the octave band past the node edge, and the band is dropped rather than squeezed.
- An ordered release is lost when a note is released before its arrival finishes; at fresh settings that is any note shorter than about 0.45 s. You chose that trade in #894.

---

## Stars texture (Analyzer and Lattice)

### Questions

1. **Is the fresh Stars look still the one you want?**
   It is your 2026-09-26 DAW capture (#1205) replayed through four later changes:
   - #1234 made Position variation default to 50% (it was 100% when captured);
   - #1248 shortened and reduced the far three layers' glow;
   - #1260 made Star softness widen every depth equally (the captured 35% used to widen only the nearest stars);
   - #1279 made Medium the default quality.
   Medium draws the nearest halo at 45% resolution, below the "half resolution is the minimum acceptable" recorded in #1234.
   - *Yes:* record "fresh Stars, Medium included, is intended".
   - *No:* re-capture the Stars dials and quality from your current project with `capture-daw-state`.
2. **Should the near end of Star size make near stars visibly bigger?**
   Core width scales by `(near/far ÷ 16)^depth`, so near stars grow only when the range spans more than 16×.
   At the fresh 2.3 → 14.8 px (6.4×) the nearest cores come out about the same width as the far dust (σ ≈ 0.60 against 0.58). The near stars are sparser, with wider halo reach, not bigger.
   The hover says the near handle sets "the biggest stars".
   - *Yes:* make core size follow the size range directly (a look change, needs a render round).
   - *No:* reword the hover to say the handle mostly sets near spacing.
3. **Do you want more headroom above the fresh Star density and Halo strength?**
   Both fresh values sit at the top of their bars (density 10×, Halo strength 50%).
   The Halo cap's reason ("past half … a flat wash") dates from a 1.2-cell reach that #1248 shortened to 0.85 cells for the far layers.
   - *Yes:* widen both limits and check the atlas budget at the new top.
   - *No:* record that the limits are fine.
4. **Is Uniform a reference view whose speed on large panes doesn't matter?**
   Uniform alone keeps a "native split" path above 2560×1440 px, with its own shader branches, test hook and threshold.
   The threshold was measured against the walk renderer #1234 replaced, and has not been re-measured since. #1142 lists that as open.
   - *Yes:* drop Uniform's split, so Uniform always draws unsplit (removes the threshold, hook, a test and two shader branches).
   - *No:* re-measure the cutoff on the current renderer, under #1142.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1306; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- Dragging Star speed, Drift direction or Star lifetime re-lays the whole field, because position and life are computed from the total clock.
- Uniform differs from the three presets in look as well as cost: the presets shorten distant halos by Position variation.

---

## Video: takes and offline export

### Questions

1. **Has "Transport stop" been finishing your Bitwig audio exports correctly?**
   The UI and the guide disagree about this.
   The At bar hover says it is "the one that works during an audio export" (`panes/render.rs:600`), and its doc says Transport stop's debounce is "the wrong clock".
   `docs/offline-rendering.md:150` says to use Transport stop for exports.
   #523 made Transport stop work on real Bitwig takes. #817 added At bar and restated Transport stop as unusable, yet its own body says At bar is "unverified in Bitwig" during an export. #848 then made stopped-host exports finish on the playhead restore.
   - *Yes:* rewrite the At bar hover as "end at a chosen bar", without "the one that works".
   - *No:* file the failing case, and point the guide at At bar.
2. **Should an auto-rendered take use the Aspect and Output size set when you armed it, like the rest of its look?**
   Today the automatic render passes the Aspect and Output size set when recording *stops* (`record/recorder/render_job.rs:26`). A change mid-take gives a recomposed video and a warning about a `--size` flag you never typed.
   The reason for passing the size went away in #152, when the renderer began reading the size from the take. #797 kept it as "the existing stop-time resolution override".
   - *Yes:* stop passing it (Re-render still applies the current settings).
   - *No:* keep it, and rewrite both comments to state the real reason.
3. **Do you ever pass `--layout side-by-side` or `--layout stacked` when rendering a take by hand?**
   These presets are frozen from before the captured frame (lattice-left 68%, lattice-top 74%). #974 retired the single-pane presets but kept these two as "not separately established as unused".
   - *Yes:* keep them and fix their comment.
   - *No:* remove `--layout` and the presets, and move the determinism fixture to a test-only constructor, as #990 did.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1307; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- `align.rs`, `--align` and `--audio` are gone (#903, #983, #1214), and the retired flags are refused with a clear error.
- "Fit video (max 10 min)" silently caps history at 600 s, so the last frame of a longer video doesn't reach back to its start.
- Re-render appears only after a take finishes in this session, and targets the most recent take. After a reload, the command line is the only way back.
- "Manually" with a looping transport splits the take at each rewind, and renders only the last pass. That is by design since 7b3722f.

---

## Spectrogram textures (Mosaic, Watercolor, Scales, softness, contours)

### Questions

1. **Should the Level contours block grey out while Stars is at 100% Texture mix?**
   Stars has been the fresh style since #1205. Under it, Contour strength, levels and edge softness change nothing on screen, yet the block stays live, against the page's rule that a row whose effect is off is greyed (#928).
   The Stars hover already says contours don't apply.
   Below 100% Texture mix the plain picture under the stars *is* terraced, so it is only the 100% case.
   - *Yes:* grey the block under Stars at 100%, and skip the contour work in the shader there.
   - *No:* leave it live; fix only the comments that say contours never reach Stars.
2. **Should a fresh project start with contours off?**
   Contour strength 100% with 16 soft levels is fresh because "the Lava style was the fresh one" (`atmosphere.rs:629`).
   Lava is gone, and #1205 captured the value while Stars hid it.
   So a new project that switches from Stars to Mosaic, Watercolor or Scales opens terraced.
   The same applies to the colour response (0.04/0.71 s) and drift (4.2×) values captured under Stars.
   - *Yes:* default Contour strength to 0%.
   - *No:* keep 100%, and replace the Lava rationale with "your call, 2026-09-29".

### Mechanical

Filed as #1308; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- The textures come from a baked 40-cell tile (#999). At fresh sizes Mosaic repeats about every 23% of the pane height and Watercolor about every 14%, under a picture that mostly hides it.
- Dragging Drift speed or direction re-places the texture by the elapsed clock, and resets colour memory. This is the stated design, since drift is `clock × speed`.

---

## Spectrum analyzer and audio analysis

Nearly everything here traces to one change: #1205 moved the fresh analysis window from Balanced to Fast (8192 → 4096 samples) and History from 171 s to 39 s.
Tests that used the defaults were pinned to the old Balanced window rather than re-examined, so nothing tests the window you ship.

### Questions

1. **At the Fast default, is a pure tone's ridge sitting up to about 23¢ off its note ribbon at A4 fine (more in the bass)?**
   Peaks and ridges land on FFT bins, since peak refinement was removed on purpose.
   The only peak-placement test pins Balanced *because* Fast "draws [A4] on its nearest bin, about 21¢ sharp" (`ui/tests/spectrum.rs:9`).
   The window hint says only "coarse bass pitch".
   - *Yes:* record it, and reword the hint to "coarse pitch, especially in the bass".
   - *No:* make Balanced the fresh window again.
2. **With the audio ring on, is losing its lowest wedge below about C4 acceptable at Fast?**
   The ring's noise floor is a median over ±150¢. It was sized at Balanced, where it "eats the fundamental" only around C2 (`panes/spectral_fold.rs:94`).
   At Fast the bins are twice as wide, so it eats fundamentals up to roughly C4: bass notes light only from their harmonics.
   Every fold test pins Balanced or Precise. This is arithmetic from the doc's own formula, not a measurement, and the ring is off in a fresh view.
   - *Yes:* correct the doc to Fast, add Fast to the gate test, and record the decision.
   - *No:* scale the floor's window with the FFT window, checked against a Fast fixture first.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1309; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- Changing Frequency resolution or Spectrum averaging leaves already-drawn history as it was, so the spectrogram becomes a patchwork until it scrolls out. Tilt, level windows and gradient do re-map old history.
- Double-clicking Frequency range or Spectrum level range resets to the full extent (20 Hz–20 kHz, -100–0 dB), not to the fresh values.
- The docked divider's saved share (85% history) is what the Video preview and the export compose from, whatever the editor currently shows after a resize.

---

## Lattice shadows and the idle lattice

### Questions

1. **Should "Idle ring brightness" move out of Idle lattice, renamed for what it colours?**
   A lattice with nothing playing draws only crosses: no node is sent to the GPU unless something lights it (`render/lattice_frame.rs:179`). So this bar changes nothing at rest.
   It colours the silent octave slices of sounding or fading nodes, and the audio ring's quiet end.
   It began as one "Ground" bar (#393), when grid, audio ring and MIDI ring were the whole lattice at rest. #429 replaced the grid with crosses, which have their own bar, and #628 renamed Ground without moving it.
   - *Yes:* move it to Note layers as something like "Silent slice brightness", and rewrite the hovers.
   - *No:* keep it, and fix the prose (`panes/plus.rs:5`) that says rings are part of the idle picture.
2. **Should the Analyzer's shadows use Darkness the way the Lattice's do?**
   The Lattice darkens by `darkness × coverage` (#866, #1164). The Analyzer's ribbons, dots and labels still darken in stops, `(1 − darkness)^coverage`.
   That stops curve came in with #446 under the rule "every Shadow group spends its depth by the same curve", which the comment still states.
   #1164 moved the lattice's labels and crosses to linear darkening, and said only that the analyzer shadows "keep their existing compositing".
   At your 91% Analyzer darkness, a Blur tail at 30% coverage darkens about 51% under stops, and about 27% under linear.
   The Shadow profile preview draws the linear curve on both pages.
   - *Yes:* switch the Analyzer to linear darkening. Its shadow tails get shorter and lighter, so you re-dial.
   - *No:* keep stops there, fix the "same curve" and "STOPS" prose, and make the Analyzer page's preview draw its real curve.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1310; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- Under Label visibility "All", every home-sheet position is named, so the whole cross field disappears (a name replaces its cross).
- #570 (cross taper clips the shadow) was closed as not seen in use. Both defects are still in the shader, and the fresh cross shadow is now Blur, the variant that applies the taper twice.

---

## Tuning, lattice maps and adaptive tuning

### Questions

1. **With the engine on Pass through, should Learn move the lattice axes even when a Tune row has Retune ticked?**
   Learn freezes the fifth, third and seventh whenever any live source has Retune on, since the lattice is then the retuning target.
   The test counts Retune flags only (`plugin/tuning/hub.rs:1192`), not the engine. Tunes default to Retune on, so in Pass through, with nothing being retuned, Learn still only moves the C offset.
   - *Yes:* ignore Retune while the engine is Pass through.
   - *No:* record it.

### Bug

Filed as #1302.

- **"Learning unavailable … Reset to recover" does not recover when you press Reset.**
  Once Learn is armed and a source's held state goes incomplete, the configuration owner latches a status bit (`plugin/configuration.rs:437`), and Learn stays off.
  Only a host reset or reactivation clears it (`:262`). The pane's "Reset all voices" doesn't.
  #709 had a second clearer, which #788 deleted, while writing "a fault is a status bit rather than a gate". `hub.rs:1196` says "nothing latches".
  The test that names this case (`tuning/confirmed_tests.rs:63`) never arms Learn, so it can't reach the latch.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1311; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- A fresh Harmonigraph passes its own input through: its own Retune is off (#819), and a Tune's is on.
- Projects saved during #858's two-hour window may still carry a 1 s Half-life, which #860 measured as failing the shuttle case. The value is on screen, so a quick look at Adaptive → Half-life would tell.
- The Assignments list spells notes with sharps (D♯) and Last attack with flats (E♭).

---

## Editor shell, layout and saved state

### Questions

1. **Do you still use Tab / Hide tab bars now that videos come from the offline renderer?**
   It was added (b706c01a3) so that "the lattice flows straight into the Spectral pane for clean captures", which was screen-recording videos.
   The offline renderer never reads it, and #1056 kept it with "frameless mode … remain(s)" and no reason.
   It takes Tab away from egui's focus walk, reasoning "nothing here is driven from the keyboard", which stopped being true with #1278's arrow-key handles.
   With the bars hidden, a folded pane disappears and nothing on screen can unfold it.
   - *Yes:* keep it, move it to the editor-only preferences, and rewrite its three comments.
   - *No:* remove the setting, the Tab handler and its branches.

### Bug

Filed as #1301.

- **A project saved with the editor open stores the settings from the last time the editor closed.**
  The UI state blob is written only in the editor window's `Drop` (`plugin/editor/window.rs:288`), and `background.rs:705` documents it.
  So Bitwig saving while the window is open writes the previous close's appearance, layout and camera, or nothing if the editor was never closed this session.
  This breaks the "value on screen is the value the file holds" contract.
  It is found by reading, not yet reproduced in Bitwig.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1312; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- No compat shims were found. VST3 removal (#1185) is complete.
- Folding or unfolding a pane resizes the plugin window by the freed amount, down to 400×300.
- Value bars have no double-click reset (double-click types a value). The range, stack and layer widgets reset on double-click instead.

---

## Spiral

### Questions

1. **Should the Spiral's note dots be about a quarter larger, as their own sizing rule intends?**
   The dot size rule (a 0.7 share of the track, a 3 pt floor) describes a disc that used to include a black ring.
   #610 replaced the ring with the shadow and kept its 1.25 pt inset "as the established body size" (`panes/spiral.rs:140`).
   So on a 400 pt pane the rule gives about 5.6 pt and the drawn dot is about 4.35 pt.
   - *Yes:* drop the inset, so dots draw at the ruled size.
   - *No:* restate the rule's constants so they describe the drawn dot, with the same pixels.

### Mechanical

Filed as #1313; nothing there needs your call.

### Notable, no decision needed

- The Spiral shares the Analyzer's Frequency range, so at the fresh range a note below about F2 gets no dot and no name.
- The ribbons' Show note names and Label scale don't apply to the Spiral's rim names. That has been so since #375.
- Dots ignore the Opacity mapping; that question sits in the Colors section.

---

## Method notes

- Cost: 22 agents (opus auditors, sonnet describers), about 5.2M subagent tokens, run 4–10 agents at a time.
- What found things:
  - fresh defaults first; the #1205 capture explains findings in six areas;
  - tracing a PR that changed a field's meaning (#1133 made `activation` carry opacity; #1205 moved the FFT window) to every reader of that field;
  - scoping lines ("keep", "remain", "retains") in removal PRs.
- Noise: removed-identifier sweeps, about half hits.
- The textures auditor's test sweep finished after its hand-back and was folded in.
title: Drift audit 2026-09-29: all areas (21 questions)

body:
A dense full-cap spectrogram refold can stall the UI during long-Span interaction. Measured while addressing the performance-evidence finding on PR #884: https://github.com/yan-h/harmonigraph/pull/884. The implementation is correct, but the earlier 5.80 ms CPU number used only two active bins and 256 slabs; most output quantizations took the cheap floor branch.

Reproduction (temporary release unit probe inside `harmonigraph-ui/src/spectrogram.rs`, alongside the aggregator tests):

1. Build `SpectrumHistory::default()` by pushing 65,536 `SpectrogramColumn::from_power` values at `(i as f64 + 0.5) * 0.008` seconds, with every one of the 3,828 power bins set to `1e-10_f32` (-100 dB, above the -120 dB floor).
2. Assert history contains 7,168 stored columns, represented counts `{1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}`, and total represented count 65,536. This exercises the real coarsening path.
3. For every timed repetition create a fresh `SpectrogramAgg::new()` and black-box `agg.window(&history, 0, 0.512, ring_slots(1024))`. Timing ends only after `window` returns its owned grid, including the final quantization and partial-first-slab repair/readout. Exclude fixture creation and validation.
4. Outside the timer assert 1,024 centers, 3,919,872 nonzero bytes all equal to `quantize(1e-10)`, no held slabs, and `grid.dirty == false`. The window is 524.288 seconds, within the 600-second live range.
5. Run release mode with two warmups and eleven measured repetitions. A second run used the already-built test executable without concurrent local compilation or GPU probes.

Measured locally on Apple Silicon, 2026-09-14:

- Initial full refold: median 80.510 ms, min 32.168 ms, max/p95 195.465 ms.
- Isolated repeat: median 60.120 ms, min 26.982 ms, max/p95 94.688 ms.

These small, variable headless runs do not establish production tail latency. They do show that even the fastest observed full-cap refold exceeds a 60 Hz frame budget before other UI/GPU work.

The synchronous call path is spectral-pane drawing → `run_for` → `build` → `SpectrogramAgg::window`. Rebuild triggers include first display of existing history, Span or pane/display-density changes crossing the held slab-width rung, coverage reaching behind retained slabs, and backward source time. Unchanged-rung arrivals remain incremental; palette/style/pitch-range edits do not inherently rebuild.

What the investigation eliminated:

- This CPU probe includes no GPU work, shader compilation, or readback waits.
- It is not a cached window hit: each full-refold repetition starts with a fresh aggregator.
- It is not silence, a tiny slab fixture, fake coarse counts, or unfinalized output: the assertions above cover these cases.
- No approximation or fast-log change was tried. The temporary probes are removed after measurement; PR #884 retains the raw evidence in `docs/evidence/spectrogram-lava/performance.txt` and corrects the performance claim.

Likely work by inspection: 27,439,104 f32-to-f64 additions reading roughly 105 MiB of history, plus 3,919,872 non-floor logarithmic quantizations and about 3.74 MiB of grid readout. A follow-up should use the measured breakdown to evaluate a bounded refold-latency improvement while preserving power averaging, quantization, and incremental cache correctness. Avoid widening cache keys or silently changing the displayed calibration.

Bounded follow-up stage probe (same dense history/slab dimensions, two warmups and eleven measurements): rebuild plus finalization median 29.542 ms (22.475–48.641); subsequent actual view/readout median 0.142 ms. Standalone existing accumulator calls: add all 7,168 columns median 10.110 ms, write 1,024 dense slabs median 14.852 ms. These separate microprobes are indicative, not additive attribution. Across 128 subsequent dense arrivals, timing allocation/history push/full incremental window readout gave median 0.178 ms, p95 0.756 ms, maximum 3.143 ms; asserted only the initial rebuild occurred. Folding and non-floor quantization dominate; copying is much smaller. No simple safe optimization was identified in the bounded review follow-up.
title: Dense full-cap spectrogram refolds can hitch during Span and resize changes
